summary: The stop was rejected again, so I used the remaining interval on the account with the fewest executions behind its decisive observation. The heartbeat question's term-inversion rate rests on two runs of its fsync harness, 89 and 69 inversions across 200 attempts each with mean writes near 2.0 and 2.5 ms, while its zero-delay contrast comes from four jitter runs that recorded 0, 0, 2 and 1. I requested a third execution of cc2661ee13b14149b7ca04c9d5a35509-experiment from its retained inputs, which reruns the same cases, admissions and assertions with no code change. A rate in the same band turns the measured exposure into a three-point range and leaves the account's conclusion, its five counterevidence items and its platform caveats exactly as recorded, including that neither run varies the storage stack or the sync mode; a rate well outside that band would reopen the claim that a concurrent fast-path heartbeat can leave the node below a term it had already adopted, which is the premise the whole account turns on. The request validates against the schema and makes no other edits.
